title: Grounding LLMs in Scientific Discovery via Embodied Actions
claim: Existing paradigms run code or fixed tools blindly and then respond; ours closes a continuous perception-action loop with the environment.
layout: 3 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, red critique box at right, side arrows
description: The figure has three stacked dashed-border panels. Paradigm 1 (Code-as-Action) is a gray row: an LLM agent icon, an arrow labeled Code Generation, and a MATLAB Simulation Environment box described as opaque to the agent. Paradigm 2 (API Encapsulation) is also gray. The LLM agent makes restricted calls to a block of pre-defined static APIs (API A, B, ... N), which leads by fixed function execution to the simulation environment. A red folded-note box on the right lists the flaws: disembodiment, no continuous perception, post-hoc feedback, and blindness to transient anomalies. The bottom panel is blue and shows the proposed EmbodiedAct. Its brain-inspired modules are a Strategic Planner, a Primitive Generator and a Runtime Monitor. They are linked by Plan, Feedback and Hot-Fix Loop arrows, and an asynchronous synchronization link connects them to the simulation environment. Vertical gradient arrows on both edges label the contrast: Execute-then-Response and Passive Tool Utilization versus Runtime Perception and Active Embodied Agency.
caption: Comparison of EmbodiedAct with existing paradigms. EmbodiedAct integrates executable simulation primitives and continuous runtime perception, endowing the agent with the capacity for embodied action within physical simulation environments.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown significant potential in scientific discovery but struggle to bridge the gap between theoretical reasoning and verifiable physical simulation. Existing solutions operate in a passive "execute-then-response" loop and thus lacks runtime perception, obscuring agents to transient anomalies (e.g., numerical instability or diverging oscillations). To address this limitation, we propose EmbodiedAct, a framework that transforms established scientific software into active embodied agents by grounding LLMs in embodied actions with a tight perception-execution loop. We instantiate EmbodiedAct within MATLAB and evaluate it on complex engineering design and scientific modeling tasks. Extensive experiments show that EmbodiedAct significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving SOTA performance by ensuring satisfactory reliability and stability in long-horizon simulations and enhanced accuracy in scientific modeling.
